Variants.Content: House Reed rules the crannogmen of the Neck from Greywater Watch. It is said that Greywater Watch is built upon a floating island whose position shifts with the waterways, reeds, and bogs, so that even ravens cannot reliably find it. Their sigil is a black lizard-lion on a grey-green field; the frog spears, nets, poisoned arrows, and marsh lore of the crannogmen seem unchivalrous to southern knights, yet are perfectly suited to a land that swallows horses and heavy armor. House Reed's loyalty to House Stark comes from ancient oaths of the Neck and shared memory, needing no proof through the courtly ceremonies of the south.

Northern lords have rarely set foot in Greywater Watch, yet they know why the Neck remains the bolt across the door of the North. The Reeds do not win renown on tall chargers in the lists; their authority comes from waterways, mists, floating islands, and paths known only to crannogmen. Southrons mock them as small and poor, yet northmen know that a great host that offends the Neck will bleed slowly in places where it cannot even see the enemy.

Crannogmen measure a leader not by how high his hall stands, but by whether he remembers the season of rising waters, the reed beds where venomous snakes hide, and which old wooden causeway can still bear weight. The name of House Reed is as hard for outsiders to pin down as Greywater Watch itself; to those who live in the swamps, that is not mystery, but the common sense that keeps children alive to grow up.

Entry House Reed Lords of Greywater Watch and the crannogmen of the Neck, bearing a black lizard-lion on a grey-green field as their sigil. Their strength comes from marsh waterways, guerrilla craft, crannog culture, and ancient loyalty to House Stark; their house words are unknown. The family crest is just a facade, the real weight of the family is whether they can protect their fiefdom, honor their engagements, and rally people in times of crisis.
